content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged axolotl frame. Host frame: the axolotl sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature combining an axolotl and a Chinese pangolin. The head is that of the axolotl, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: axolotl body and legs, with its own smooth, moist skin on the face and belly, plain coat with no stripes or spots; from the Chinese pangolin, as parts and materials on the axolotl's own body, large overlapping keratin scales in its own colors, grown from the skin as the axolotl's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, hips, legs, and tail. It replaces the axolotl's smooth, moist skin there and conforms to the axolotl's body, each scale sized to the axolotl's own body segments and muscle masses, one scale per segment or muscle mass. Every covered part keeps the axolotl's own length and shape, and the tail stays the axolotl's own tail; the smooth, moist skin stops at the covering's edge, and the face and belly keep the axolotl's own smooth, moist skin. The covering follows the body's own shape. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (river forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Researching pangolin scale details**
I'm looking up reference images of Chinese pangolin scales to capture their shape, overlap, and texture so the hybrid creature's body covering is accurate before generating the illustration.
**Generating natural history illustration**
I'm creating the final watercolor and pencil illustration in a side three-quarter view, with feathery gills, countershaded scales, and a light background to match the natural history style.
**Refining illustration details**
I'm adjusting the illustration to keep the belly smooth and visible, move scales to the back and legs only, and preserve the clean natural-history style for the final version.
